facility_roles.note: The CERN Courier article on the Baksan Neutrino Observatory places SAGE at Baksan.
facility_roles.quote: This idea was implemented in two experiments: GALLEX in the Gran Sasso National Laboratory and SAGE at Baksan.

intervals.label: commissioning (gallium extractions, background reduction)
intervals.note: Start is the year extractions began on about 30 tons of gallium (SAGE 1999 paper, arXiv:astro-ph/9907113); end is the December 1989 start of solar-neutrino measurements stated in the SAGE Collaboration's 2009 paper (arXiv:0901.2200). Replaces an earlier 'construction / start' row (1989-12 to 1990-01) taken from a secondary summary, which the collaboration papers do not support as a construction period.
intervals.quote: Extractions on approximately 30 tons of Ga began in 1988; by late 1989 backgrounds were low enough to begin solar neutrino measurements.

intervals.label: primary data-taking
intervals.note: December 2007 is the end of the dataset analysed in the SAGE Collaboration's 2009 paper (arXiv:0901.2200), not a stop of data-taking; the next row records that measurements continued.
intervals.quote: For all SAGE data from January 1990 through December 2007 (168 runs and 310 separate counting sets)

intervals.label: continued operations
intervals.note: The SAGE Collaboration's 2009 paper (arXiv:0901.2200) says measurements have continued since December 1989. The only later evidence read is a CERN Courier report of 19 May 2017 ('ultra-pure gallium is still used in the SAGE experiment'); no source read confirms operation after that. Left open (`end: null`, ongoing at `verified_at` per §2.3) rather than asserting either a firm shutdown or firm continuation.
intervals.quote: Measurements have continued with only a few brief interruptions since that time.

quantity.note: 50 t is the mass stated in the SAGE Collaboration's 2009 paper (arXiv:0901.2200). The target mass varied over time: the 1999 SAGE paper (arXiv:astro-ph/9907113) says the extraction mass was increased to nearly 60 tons in summer 1991.
quantity.quote: The mass of gallium used in SAGE at the present time is 50 tonnes.

name: SAGE
notes: No dedicated official SAGE/Baksan website was reachable (inr.ru/baksan.html returned 404); no website is recorded.

physics_goals.locator: SAGE Collaboration 2009 paper (arXiv:0901.2200), abstract; CERN Courier, "Baksan scales new neutrino heights" (19 May 2017)
physics_goals.note: The paper's abstract states that SAGE measures the solar neutrino capture rate with a gallium metal target. That the gallium reaction reaches the low-energy (pp) neutrinos is stated in the same paper (233 keV threshold, sensitive to all components of the solar neutrino flux; see unique_capabilities) and by the CERN Courier article ('to detect the low-energy solar neutrinos').
physics_goals.quote: The Russian-American experiment SAGE began to measure the solar neutrino capture rate with a target of gallium metal in December 1989.
physics_goals.value: Measure the solar neutrino capture rate with a gallium metal target, via the radiochemical gallium-to-germanium reaction that reaches the low-energy (pp-chain) neutrinos

summary.plain: An experiment deep inside a Russian mountain that uses tonnes of liquid gallium metal to catch the Sun's lowest-energy neutrinos.
summary.technical: Radiochemical liquid-gallium solar-neutrino experiment at the Baksan Neutrino Observatory, Russia, under a rock overburden equivalent to 4700 m of water; 50 t gallium target. Measured a solar neutrino capture rate of 67.2 (+7.2/−7.0 stat) (+3.5/−3.0 syst) SNU over 1990-1997, about half the Standard Solar Model prediction of 129 SNU.

unique_capabilities.note: Quote states sensitivity to all components of the solar neutrino flux (including pp) because of the 233 keV threshold; 'lowest-energy (pp)' in the value is the reading that follows from that.
